tests.prompt: Add Playwright E2E tests for our Next.js app's login and 'create project' flow. Login is email + password; projects are saved through /api/projects.
tests.good: Detects existing config or proposes one with webServer, trace on-first-retry and CI retries; logs in once in a setup project and reuses storageState, with one dedicated login-UI test; role/label locators; web-first assertions and waits on the /api/projects response, no waitForTimeout; keeps the app's own API real with unique test data; stubs only third parties; tests run independently in parallel; gives the run command and how to read a trace.

tests.prompt: test_checkout_applies_discount fails about 1 in 10 CI runs but always passes on my machine. Here's the CI error: AssertionError: expected order total 90.00, got 100.00 (the discount row lookup returned another test's code).
tests.good: Doesn't skip, retry or raise timeouts; classifies as identifier collision or shared-state ordering from the error; looks for low-resolution or hard-coded discount codes and sibling tests sharing them; fixes at the source (unique per-test codes, factory) and sweeps the file; explains that local passes don't verify and proposes CI verification (baseline vs fix runs); states confidence.

tests.prompt: Write tests for this Python function that parses and formats ISO durations like 'PT1H30M' into seconds and back.
tests.good: Watches tests fail first or explains the TDD order; example tests with hand-derived expected values and named edge cases (zero, missing parts, invalid strings raise); a property-based roundtrip test (Hypothesis) offered or used if installed, with generators building valid durations rather than filtering; no tautological assertions; pytest parametrize with ids; runs the suite and reports results.

tests.prompt: Add Playwright E2E tests for the signup and checkout flows of our Next.js shop and run them on every pull request in GitHub Actions, split across four machines. The checkout form must also pass an accessibility check.
tests.good: States a short plan first: test-strategy.md and playwright-e2e.md here; the workflow through cloud-devops (ci-cd.md: least-privilege permissions, pinned actions, cached dependencies, a four-way shard matrix, reports uploaded on failure); the accessibility check through frontend-ui-design (accessibility.md: labelled inputs, a full keyboard path, visible focus). Role-based locators, web-first assertions, no fixed waits; storageState auth and unique test data; payments stubbed; shard reports merged and traces kept on retry; watches each test fail first; runs it in CI or says it couldn't; checks the Done means of all three crafts.

tests.prompt: We have a Postman collection for our orders API (create order, get order, cancel order). Add proper tests to it and make it run on every pull request in GitHub Actions against our staging API. Our Postman API key and the staging login token must not end up in the repo.
tests.good: Adds pm.test scripts per request that check status code, response schema and key fields with pm.expect, plus a response-time bound, not only 200s; chains the created order id through collection or environment variables so requests run in order and each run creates its own data; uses the current runner (Postman CLI `postman collection run`, or Newman with a JUnit or CLI reporter) with the right flags for environment file and iteration data, and states which one it chose; keeps the Postman API key and staging token in GitHub Actions secrets referenced by name and exported as environment variables, with an environment file holding placeholders only; the workflow uses least-privilege permissions, pinned action versions, uploads reports on failure, and targets staging, never production; says that cancel/delete requests mutate data and asks before running them against anything but a disposable environment; shows the run command and its real output, including failures.

tools.name: Playwright
tools.why: Most used E2E framework in the TestGuild AG2026 survey (45.1%) and 52% usage / 91% satisfaction in State of JS 2025; docs now include Test Agents and MCP.

tools.name: Selenium
tools.why: Second most used E2E tool (22.1%) in the TestGuild AG2026 survey and the enterprise and multi-language standard; the sweep found no mention in the guides.

tools.name: Cypress
tools.why: 14.4% usage in TestGuild AG2026 and 41% in State of JS 2025; large installed base of JS teams.

tools.name: Jest
tools.why: Still the most used JS test runner (about 64% in State of JS 2025) though satisfaction is falling; docs show v30.5.

tools.name: Vitest
tools.why: State of JS 2025 shows about 52-58% usage with 96% satisfaction and +14 points growth; docs now at v5.

tools.name: pytest
tools.why: The standard Python test runner with 1,300+ plugins; docs show pytest 9.

tools.name: Postman
tools.why: Default API testing and collection tool; official Claude connector and Claude Code plugin from Postman; the guides have no API-collection workflow.

tools.name: Appium
tools.why: The cross-platform standard for native mobile UI automation (TestGuild 2026 category list); docs describe Appium 3 under the OpenJS Foundation; official Appium MCP server exists.

tools.name: BrowserStack
tools.why: Leading real-device and cross-browser cloud (3,000+ devices and browsers per TestGuild); official MCP server covers Automate, App Automate, Test Management, Accessibility.

tools.name: Maestro
tools.why: 15.9k-star YAML UI-flow framework for mobile and web, now the simple alternative to Appium; official docs cover Studio, CLI and Cloud.

tools.name: Storybook
tools.why: About 30% usage in State of JS 2025; its test addon runs render, interaction, accessibility and visual tests on stories via Vitest and Chromatic.

tools.name: Testing Library
tools.why: The default way to test React and other UI components with Vitest or Jest; query by role and label as in this craft's locator rule.

tools.name: Testcontainers
tools.why: Standard way to run real databases and brokers in integration tests across Java, .NET, Go, Node and Python.

tools.name: Chrome DevTools MCP
tools.why: 52k-star official Chrome team server: navigate, emulate, inspect network and console, run Lighthouse; ships its own skills.

tools.name: Jira
tools.why: Default bug tracker and the host of the Jira-native test management apps (Zephyr, Xray): 46% of all developers use Jira in the Stack Overflow 2025 survey, and test-management round-ups say Zephyr Scale and Xray dominate Jira shops; QA issue reports usually land there. Where most teams keep bugs and test cases (Xray, Zephyr add-ons); Atlassian ships an official remote MCP server and a Claude connector.

tools.name: TestRail
tools.why: Market leader in test case management: 6sense puts it at about 41% of the test-management category (TestLink 21%, qTest 9%), and every 2026 round-up (TestRail, PractiTest, Kualitee) lists it first with Zephyr and Xray; QA teams import cases from it and push automated results to it.

tools.name: JUnit
tools.why: Default Java test framework: 84% of Java developers use JUnit (Mockito 46%) in JetBrains' State of Developer Ecosystem; the official guide is now at JUnit 6.1, while the unit-runners guide still says JUnit 5.

tools.name: Katalon
tools.why: Low-code all-in-one suite common with manual-to-automation QA teams; Katalon's 2025 State of Software Quality report (1,400+ QA respondents) names Selenium, Postman, Katalon and Cucumber as the top tools teams use, though the source is the vendor itself.
